questions.question:
In the namespace `secret-room` create a ServiceAccount named `hidden-user` that does **not** automatically mount its API token.

Verify it by creating a Pod in the same namespace that uses this ServiceAccount: the Pod must run without an API token mounted.

verification.description: ServiceAccount hidden-user exists in namespace secret-room
The ServiceAccount hidden-user has automountServiceAccountToken: false
A Pod using hidden-user runs without an automatic token mount

questions.question:
Use an AppArmor profile that denies writing to `/tmp`.

The profile `k8s-deny-write` is prepared in `/etc/apparmor.d/deny-tmp-write` on the worker node `{{NODE01}}`. Load it on `{{NODE01}}`, then update the Pod manifest `/tmp/exam/mhagou-004-q2/pod.yaml` so that its container is confined by this profile, and deploy the Pod `hello-apparmor` in the namespace `write-guard`.

The Pod must run on `{{NODE01}}`. Try to write a file to `/tmp` inside the container: it must fail, while writing elsewhere keeps working.

verification.description: AppArmor profile k8s-deny-write is loaded on {{NODE01}}
Pod hello-apparmor runs on {{NODE01}} confined by a custom AppArmor profile in enforce mode
Writing to /tmp is denied inside the Pod while other paths stay writable

questions.question:
Create a custom seccomp profile that **logs** (but does not block) the `mkdir` and `mkdirat` syscalls, and apply it to a Pod.

- The Pod `audit-pod` in the namespace `syscall-lab` runs on the worker node `{{NODE02}}` without a profile. Its manifest is `/tmp/exam/mhagou-004-q3/pod.yaml`.
- Create the profile in the kubelet seccomp directory of `{{NODE02}}` (`/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp`, which does not exist yet). It must allow every syscall; only `mkdir` and `mkdirat` are logged.
- Re-create `audit-pod` from the manifest so that it uses the profile as a `Localhost` seccomp profile.

Then run `mkdir` in the container: it must succeed and the kernel of `{{NODE02}}` must log it.

verification.description: A seccomp profile on {{NODE02}} logs mkdir and mkdirat and allows everything else
Pod audit-pod runs on {{NODE02}} with a Localhost seccomp profile that exists, and mkdir works in it
The kernel of {{NODE02}} logs the mkdir calls of the Pod

questions.question:
Falco runs as a systemd service on the worker node `{{NODE02}}` (service `falco-modern-bpf`). Its rule `Terminal shell in container` detects a shell that is opened with a terminal in a container (for example with `kubectl exec -it`).

Change the Falco rules on `{{NODE02}}` so that, whenever such a shell is opened, Falco logs a message that contains exactly:

`CRITICAL: SHELL OPENED`

Make the running Falco service use the change (it must keep running). The Pod `shell-practice` in the namespace `shell-watch` runs on `{{NODE02}}` for you to try it.

verification.description: The message is configured in the Falco files of {{NODE02}} and the Falco service was restarted afterwards
A shell with a terminal opened in the Pod makes Falco log CRITICAL: SHELL OPENED

questions.question:
Complete the Kubernetes audit policy file `/tmp/exam/mhagou-004-q5/audit-policy.yaml` so that **all requests for Secrets** (every namespace, every user, every verb) are logged at the `Metadata` level.

The policy must use `apiVersion: audit.k8s.io/v1` and `kind: Policy`. Only the policy file has to be written: you do not need to configure or restart the kube-apiserver.

verification.description: get, list and watch of Secrets are logged at Metadata
create, update, patch and delete of Secrets are logged at Metadata
Secret requests of every namespace and user are logged at Metadata
